teams.heading: Fiji Men's Sevens team partners with Coca-Cola on collectable cans
teams.body: The Fiji Men's Sevens squad is set to be featured on limited-edition Coca-Cola cans and bottles across the country. Officially launched at Albert Park in Suva, the commemorative collectable packs celebrate eight memorable moments from the national side's 2025 campaigns at the Hong Kong and Singapore tournaments. Fiji Rugby commercial director Tevita Tuiloa welcomed the initiative, noting: 'It is about celebrating our partnership, our shared memories and the special relationship between rugby and the people of Fiji.' The campaign aims to inspire young players nationwide.

lead.why: Coca-Cola has launched a new limited-edition Fiji Sevens partnership with commemorative cans and bottles in Suva.

teams.heading: Henry Slade opens up on managing diabetes during his England career
teams.body: England centre Henry Slade has spoken openly about the reality of managing Type one diabetes throughout his professional career. Diagnosed at 18, the Exeter Chiefs midfielder admitted the diagnosis was a 'tough pill to swallow' but was inspired by his father, John, who also has the condition. Slade, now a key figure in Steve Borthwick's national set-up, revealed he never doubted his ability to play rugby at the highest level despite the daily challenges of regulating his blood sugar.

teams.heading: Ireland women cruise past Japan in Cork for second consecutive victory
teams.body: The Ireland women's national team overcame an early deficit to beat Japan 43-19 at Virgin Media Park in Cork. After conceding a rolling-maul try in the opening minutes, the hosts utilised their superior scrum dominance to win penalties and territory. Flyhalf Dannah O'Brien's tactical kicking constantly troubled the visitors' back field, while Aoife Dalton gained crucial metres with every carry. The victory completes a back-to-back double over the visitors, following a 31-24 win in Galway.

The team's biggest victory during this period of matches came in November 2025 in the International Friendlies, when they beat Chile 34-19 at home.

teams.heading: Scottish Rugby concussion lawsuit faces collapse over unpaid legal costs
teams.body: The landmark brain injury litigation against World Rugby and UK governing bodies, including Scottish Rugby, faces a sudden threat of collapse. Claimants pursuing the case must settle a £2.8 million legal bill this month to proceed. This financial hurdle comes after the governing bodies lost their court battle in August to have the brain injury cases thrown out. The multi-million-pound costs now present a critical obstacle for the claimants.

teams.heading: Wales hooker Dewi Lake captains Gloucester in Premiership as Llewellyn returns
teams.body: Wales hooker Dewi Lake captains Gloucester in this weekend's Premiership meeting with Leicester Tigers, giving national selectors a close look at several key Test contenders. Lake is joined in the visitors' squad by returning Welsh international centre Max Llewellyn, who secures a place on the bench. The clash features a heavy Welsh presence, with Leicester starting international back-row duo Tommy Reffell and Aaron Wainwright. This derby provides vital competitive minutes for the Welsh contingent as preparation intensifies for the upcoming November internationals.

teams.heading: Argentina suffer chaotic England defeat after late TMO call rules out try
teams.body: The Pumas were left frustrated in the Nations Championship after a dramatic 31-24 defeat against England. In a chaotic third-round encounter, the hosts fell just short after a controversial late TMO decision ruled out a last-gasp try that would have offered a chance to salvage the match. The result leaves Argentina with one victory and two defeats from their first three matches of the tournament as they look ahead to their November clash against Ireland.

teams.heading: Les Kiss keeps Joseph Suaalii on wing for Bledisloe Cup opener
teams.body: Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has made only one change to his starting line-up for Saturday’s Bledisloe Cup Test against the All Blacks at Eden Park, bringing rookie Isaac Henry into the centres. Hunter Paisami’s suspension opens the door for Henry, while league convert Joseph Suaalii remains on the wing. Kiss has reverted to a 5-3 bench split, declaring, "Keeping consistency in the starting side gives us a solid foundation, while adding some freshness on the bench will provide energy late in the game."

teams.heading: Japan Sakura Sevens reclaim Asian Games gold with final win over China
teams.body: The Japan Sakura Sevens reclaimed the Asian Games gold medal by defeating defending champions China 10-5 in a tense final in Nagoya. After missing out on the title at the previous Games, the hosts fought back to secure the top step of the podium on home soil. It was a mixed campaign for the country's sevens programme overall, as the Japan men’s team suffered a surprise 10-7 semi-final defeat to China before rebounding to take bronze with a 17-5 victory over Korea.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie rules Richie Mo'unga out of both Bledisloe Cup Tests
teams.body: All Blacks coach Dave Rennie has confirmed playmaker Richie Mo'unga will miss both Bledisloe Cup Tests against Australia after tearing his calf. The injury forces a backline reshuffle for Saturday's opening Test at Eden Park, with Damian McKenzie shifting to fly-half and Beauden Barrett starting at full-back. Scott Barrett also returns from back surgery. Rennie, preparing to face his former side, brushed off suggestions of having a point to prove. 'It's not about me. You know, I've got no regrets,' he said.

teams.heading: JP Pietersen starts Eben Etzebeth and Ox Nché for URC Stormers clash
teams.body: Sharks head coach JP Pietersen has bolstered his pack for Saturday’s coastal derby by naming Springboks Eben Etzebeth and Ox Nché in the starting XV. Etzebeth earns his first start of the United Rugby Championship season following a dominant cameo against Leinster, while Nché’s inclusion shifts fellow international Thomas du Toit to tighthead. Both the league-leading Sharks and the Stormers have opted for 6-2 bench splits for the encounter, though the visitors remain without unavailable Test stars Bongi Mbonambi and Makazole Mapimpi.
